trust_decision.summary: Whether a client IP may use the mirror is decided by config.ipWhitelist, which at the pinned commit runs only as Express middleware; the Socket.IO server on the same http.Server never checks it, so any peer can emit node-helper notifications (e.g. newsfeed CHECK_ARTICLE_URL) that make the server fetch arbitrary URLs.

landing_point.why: The summary names the newsfeed Socket.IO notification and SSRF; the unvalidated fetch(url, {method: 'HEAD'}) of CHECK_ARTICLE_URL is the obvious sink.

fix_sites.entry_point: Socket.IO handshake (GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling and the websocket upgrade) via new socketIpAccessControl in js/ip_access_control.js
Socket.IO server construction in js/server.js:43 (allowRequest option), reached by every namespace io.of(name) used by node helpers
Every HTTP route behind app.use(ipAccessControl) at js/server.js:90, plus the socket handshake; resolveClientIp changes client-IP derivation (X-Forwarded-For trusted only from loopback peer)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: js/server.js:43-51 (Socket.IO options, no allowRequest) and js/ip_access_control.js:41-61 (Express-only guard), far from the newsfeed sink at defaultmodules/newsfeed/node_helper.js:28

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ipWhitelist is an HTTP middleware for serving the page, and the socket is the mirror's own internal client channel; the report is about newsfeed SSRF, so hardening the URL check in the newsfeed helper (like /cors already does) looks like the complete fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Empty ipWhitelist ([]) must still allow all IPs for both HTTP and socket; the browser/Electron client on localhost must still connect; a local reverse proxy (loopback peer) forwarding X-Forwarded-For must be judged on the forwarded client IP; and newsfeed CHECK_ARTICLE_URL / ADD_FEED must still fetch arbitrary public feed and article URLs, so a sink-level block of non-whitelisted hosts breaks legitimate feeds.

O6_input_shapes: Socket.IO handshake request (raw IncomingMessage, no req.ip) over polling
X-Forwarded-For as comma list, first entry taken, only when direct peer is loopback (127.0.0.1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1, ::1)
X-Forwarded-For ignored when direct peer is not loopback
empty or non-array whitelist means allow all

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-namespace or secondary Socket.IO server/attachment (e.g. a module-level io instance or a separate path) created without allowRequest
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Helpers already receive io and call io.of(name); a maintainer adding a debug/remote-control socket or a second http.Server (e.g. for watch mode reload) would plausibly construct it without copying the option.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an HTTP route registered before app.use(ipAccessControl) (e.g. /reload for watch mode) that emits to sockets
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Route ordering in Express is easy to get wrong when adding tooling endpoints; it would bypass the whitelist on a different transport.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: test hidden route: ADD_CALENDAR / weather INIT_WEATHER socket notifications as further server-side fetch triggers that a newsfeed-only sink fix leaves open
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already present in the real code; useful as hidden test routes that punish a solver who validates only CHECK_ARTICLE_URL.

O9_family: SSRF via missing access control on a second transport (CWE-918 / authorization bypass, Socket.IO vs Express)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/e2e/ipWhitelist_spec.js (HTTP-only 403/200 at pinned commit) with tests/configs/noIpWhiteList.js; fix adds socket handshake e2e cases and tests/unit/functions/ip_access_control_spec.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add URL/SSRF validation (protocol, private-IP block like /cors) inside newsfeed checkArticleUrl and leave the Socket.IO handshake unguarded.

out_of_scope_notes: defaultmodules/weather/node_helper.js:29-52 builds a require() path from socket-supplied weatherProvider (path.join) without validation; separate weakness, not pursued.

js/server_functions.js:101-105 /cors already has SSRF guards (DNS pin, unicast-only); socket-driven fetchers (newsfeed, calendar, weather HTTPFetcher) have none; separate defence, not this advisory's property.
